goal: Produce, for every in-scope game, an independent number (spread, total, moneyline) plus the per-player distributions needed to price props - before looking at any market price, and scored against the market's close rather than against the scoreboard.
key_constraint: The half of this pipeline that does not need purchased data is the half that can be built today: schedule, availability, depth, box-score-derived team and player baselines are all official and free. The half that needs money is only the price data. That asymmetry is the most useful single finding in this section, and it is why SG-01 is the first decision on the list.

steps.what: Every game with date, kickoff, venue, TV slot, rest days and days-since-previous game.
steps.note: Present in the repository's official snapshot for 2026, with 24 TBD kickoff rows and 49 preseason matchups without dates; the collector refresh closes the age gap.

steps.what: Turn transactions into dated unavailability (IR, NFI, PUP, suspension, commissioner exempt, practice-squad elevation windows) rather than a same-day flag.
steps.inputs: club transaction listings, league roster rules
steps.note: Rule set verified from an official (2022-era) article; the transaction source URL still needs a working endpoint (IR-028).

steps.what: Per report day: player, position, practice status, game status, exactly as published; blanks preserved as coded states.
steps.note: Schema and one full club block verified this session; the append-only history is the part that makes retrospective signals honest.

steps.what: Detect position-1 changes between consecutive charts, count listed bodies per position, mark 'no listed backup'.
steps.inputs: 32 club depth-chart pages plus their own 'Updated as of' dates
steps.note: One club verified end to end (49ers, 11/10/26). The left-corner case shows what the brief is asking for: a first-string starter with no listed second.

steps.what: Map positions to units and roles (11-man defense packages, offensive line, specialty groups) so a group-level depletion state can be computed rather than a count of names.
steps.note: Deterministic from LM-04; no new data needed.

steps.step: Team baselines from official game results
steps.what: Scoring rate, point differential, home-field and rest effects, opponent-adjusted, expressed as a distribution over margins and totals.
steps.note: The repository holds schedules and broadcast windows, not box scores. This is the largest free gap: results are official and need no purchase, and it is the input that makes an originated number possible at all.

steps.what: Snap share, route participation, targets per route, touches per available back, per position group.
steps.inputs: play-by-play (live during games) and league tracking (published the day after)
steps.note: Latency is a documented league fact, not an engineering failure: same-day modelling must rely on the depth chart and report, and must say so.

steps.what: Estimated effect on expected margin and expected total of a given unit's replacement state, fitted on history with the context controls (opponent, rest, venue, game importance) held fixed.
steps.note: The number that the brief calls 'deficiency in the defense' is this estimate; until it is fitted on data it is a formula, not a quantity.

steps.what: Expected margin and total -> spread and total with key-number and half-point grid; moneyline from the win-probability model with a stated vig; alternates from the same distribution.
steps.note: Discrete-margin handling (SG-08) is not optional: a normal-approx margin model misprices the mass at 3 and 7 by construction.

steps.what: Snapshot the market at fixed timestamps, remove vig consistently across the two sides, and record both the raw price and the devigged probability.
steps.note: The only hard-cost item in the pipeline. Without it, LM-11 and LM-12 cannot run and the site cannot show a single edge number.

steps.what: Trade only when the standardised disagreement exceeds the pre-registered threshold; skip otherwise; log every skipped candidate so the 'eligibility denominator' is real.
steps.note: Logging the skipped games is what makes the coverage statistic in gate G-14 computable.

steps.what: Settle from the official league result and the season's statistic definitions; compute outcomes, CLV, calibration and the luck budget.
steps.inputs: official results, stat standard, LM-10 closes
steps.note: Prop settlement is where definitions bite (carries, attempts, sacks, half-point rules), so the definition source is stored per season with the result.

steps.what: Each model version is pre-registered, hashed and frozen mid-season; re-fits happen on a rolling window only, and one season is held out untouched.
steps.note: Cheap, and the difference between a leaderboard and a lottery.

validation_protocol.before_any_price: Score the originated number on outcome metrics alone: Brier score and log loss on the win probability, absolute error on the spread and total against realised margins and totals, and the key-number calibration of the margin distribution. This measures prediction quality, not betting value, and it can be run entirely on free official data.
validation_protocol.once_prices_exist: Add the market comparison: mean absolute deviation from the close, the share of games where our line is closer than the close, and CLV on the signals the model would trade. Only these second-set metrics can answer 'can we beat the market'.
validation_protocol.never: Do not report a win rate, a profit figure, or a 'recovered' edge from a period in which prices were not captured at the registered cut-off, and do not compare our line against an opening price we did not actually have access to at the time.

worked_arithmetic.note: The tables on this page (vig, break-even, required sample, ROI standard error, correlation bounds) are computed by the build from the formulas shown, on the stated assumptions. They are arithmetic, not measurement, and they are labelled DERIVED everywhere they appear.
